cta.quoteHtml: Offer it. It could be your Gest Dobra.
cta.text: If tomorrow you were to make one gesture that no one would notice, reward or keep score of, what would it be — and who would you offer it to?
cta.title: One Simple Gesture
ex.e1: You could ask a waiter to add another table's meal to your bill, choosing the guests at random. When they ask for their bill, the waiter could say: “This is a Gest Dobra — a gesture of kindness. Your meal has been paid for today. You owe nothing in return. If you ever feel like doing something kind for someone else, please pass it on.” If they would rather not accept the gift, they are entirely free to pay for themselves.
ex.e2: You can share your time, knowledge or skills. Help someone with a difficult task, prepare a snack for a colleague, invite them to lunch or support them through a hard day. Sometimes all it takes is to do something kind for someone, without expecting anything in return.
ex.e3: You could chat with an older person, help with a small technical problem, fill in a form for someone, clear snow from a stretch of pavement, mow a lawn, look after your neighbours' children so they can have some time to themselves, or do something else that makes everyday life a little better for those around you.
ex.e4: You can offer a small gesture to a complete stranger: buy someone a coffee, pay for their ticket or give them a little surprise. Simply to share some kindness.
ex.lead: Gest Dobra can take a material form, but its spirit is at its purest when no one except the recipient knows about it.
ex.title: Examples of Gest Dobra
footer: Gest Dobra — accept kindness and, if you wish, pass it on.

hero.lead: Gest Dobra — Polish for “a gesture of kindness” — is a freely given act of kindness from one person to another.
hero.title: Accept kindness.
how.lead: You don't need a great deal of money or resources. One tangible act of kindness is enough, offered without expecting gratitude, recognition or payment.
how.s1: Someone has done something kind for you, with no strings attached — not because you earned it or will return the favour. Accept the gift. Perhaps one day, through you, kindness will reach someone else.
how.s1alt: Two hands passing a red heart in soft light
how.s2: Look around. Who near you needs help, time, attention or support — a simple human gesture? Perhaps there is someone you would like to be kind to for no particular reason. Or someone you know will pass that kindness on.
how.s2alt: A person sitting on a bench, paying close attention to the people around them
how.s3: Do something kind within your means, simply to give another person the chance to experience kindness. If you hand them a Gest Dobra card, it becomes a symbol of that gesture and an invitation to pass kindness on to others. That is how Gest Dobra keeps going.
how.s3alt: A person passing on a Gest Dobra card, symbolising kindness continuing its journey
how.title: How Can You Pass Gest Dobra On?
idea.c1: When someone gives us something without expecting payment, we often feel an immediate urge to return the favour. Gest Dobra interrupts that calculation. It lets us accept kindness without feeling that we have to “settle the score” straight away.
idea.c2: Gest Dobra is not reserved for those who need help, are more vulnerable or are going through a difficult time. It is for people. For everyone. It does not label, judge or divide us into categories.
idea.c3: Gest Dobra is not a marketing campaign, a discount or a promotional freebie. It might take the form of an item or service freely given, a bill paid, practical help, time, attention, standing up for someone more vulnerable or quietly solving someone's problem.
idea.c4: Kindness should not create new problems. Gest Dobra is an expression of goodwill and must not become a burden on you or your loved ones. What matters is not the size of the gesture, but the intention and the willingness to share thoughtfully, within your means.
idea.c5: A Gest Dobra cannot be demanded, obtained by manipulation or expected as an entitlement. Its essence is that it is freely given: an expression of the giver's choice and an invitation to the person receiving it.

idea.quote: “This is not a promotion or a temporary campaign. It is a principle: pass it on if you wish.”
idea.title: What Does Gest Dobra Really Mean?

sub.card.capt1: At first we need help and guidance.
sub.card.capt2: Over time we become independent and gain confidence.
sub.card.capt3: Then we can ride on and help others.
sub.card.cardsCaption: The Gest Dobra card – front and back
sub.card.frontAlt: Front of the Gest Dobra card: the logo with a heart above an open hand and the words “You may keep it or pass it on…” in Polish
sub.card.imgAlt: A journey from support to independence, symbolising the role of the Gest Dobra card
sub.card.p1: The Gest Dobra card is not an advertisement, a novelty or a keepsake. It is a tool that helps a person understand what has just happened.
sub.card.p2: It makes two things easier: accepting kindness without feeling indebted, and offering kindness without expecting a favour in return. At first, this may feel unfamiliar to many people, which is why a simple reminder of the principle can help.
sub.card.p3: Just as a child needs support when learning to walk, and a balance bike helps them learn to balance, the card helps us discover a new, more humane way of sharing kindness.
sub.card.quoteHtml: The card is not the essence of Gest Dobra. It supports the passing on of kindness. It helps each new person understand what the gesture means: kindness creates no debt, asks for no favour in return and can live on.
sub.card.title: Why Does the Card Matter?
sub.crumb.label: Breadcrumbs
sub.end.quote: Accept kindness. You owe nothing in return. If you wish, pass it on.
sub.end.text: Gest Dobra does not begin with grand declarations about changing the whole world. It begins by helping one person experience kindness differently — without debt, pressure or an account to settle.
sub.end.title: One Simple Thought
sub.faq.a1: No. There is no pressure and no deadline. You can pass kindness on when you want to and feel ready.
sub.faq.a2: No. It is not about matching the material value. What matters is your intention, your freedom to choose and offering kindness within your means.
sub.faq.a3: Yes. A gesture cannot be imposed on someone. The recipient's freedom is just as important as the giver's.
sub.faq.a4: The card provides support, especially at the beginning. It explains the gesture and helps prevent a sense of debt. It helps kindness travel further. Over time, people may learn to live by the idea without needing the card.
sub.faq.a5: Gest Dobra does not keep score or compel anyone. It simply invites you to pass kindness on. You are free to accept that invitation or not.
sub.faq.a6: Yes, as long as you expect no favour in return and respect the other person's freedom.

sub.faq.q2: Do I have to do something of equal value?
sub.faq.q3: Can someone decline a Gest Dobra?
sub.faq.q5: What if someone doesn't pass the kindness on?
sub.faq.q6: Can I offer a Gest Dobra to someone close to me?
sub.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sub.give.e1a: You pay the bill for someone at another table and leave without expecting to be thanked.
sub.give.e1b: The experience of a complete stranger offering them kindness while wanting nothing in return. A moment like that can change the way they see other people for a long time.
sub.give.e2a: After finishing your own work, you stay a little longer to help a colleague with a difficult task, even though you are under no obligation to do so.
sub.give.e2b: The feeling that they have not been left alone with their problem. They receive support, understanding and reassurance that work can be a place of kindness, not just of keeping track of duties.
sub.give.e3a: You offer to look after a neighbour's children for an afternoon, knowing they have no one close by who can give them a break.
sub.give.e3b: A moment to catch their breath and the feeling that they are not alone with everyday responsibilities. Sometimes a gesture like this gives more strength than any material help.
sub.give.e4a: You give a stranger a cinema or theatre ticket, explaining that it is a Gest Dobra and that you expect nothing in return.
sub.give.e4b: More than the chance to see a film or a play: above all, an experience of kindness with no strings attached — and perhaps, for the first time in a long while, the feeling that the world can still surprise them in a good way.
sub.give.label2: What does the other person really receive?
sub.give.lead: An object, a service or money can be a vehicle for kindness. What matters most, however, is what the gesture makes possible within the person who receives it.
sub.give.title: What Are We Really Giving Another Person?

sub.life.imgAlt: A heart with glowing branches spreading out towards other hearts
sub.life.lead: When we return a favour to the same person, the story of that act of kindness often comes to an end. Both people feel that the account has been settled. Gest Dobra points in another direction. Instead of returning kindness to the person who gave it to you, accept it, remember it and, when you are ready, pass it on.

sub.norev.p1: Gratitude is a good thing. The difficulty begins when gratitude turns into an obligation, and the kindness we received becomes the source of that obligation.
sub.norev.p2: Gest Dobra helps us distinguish gratitude from debt. You can feel grateful without having to give anything back. You have no obligation to settle the account.
sub.norev.quoteHtml: Returning the favour closes the story. Passing kindness on lets it continue and grow.
sub.norev.title: Why Doesn't Gest Dobra Ask for a Favour in Return?
sub.why.imgAlt: A comparison between kindness that creates an obligation and kindness freely given
sub.why.p1: In many relationships, doing good has begun to resemble an exchange. Help creates a sense of obligation, a favour calls for another in return, and a gift can feel like the beginning of an unspoken debt.
sub.why.p2: As a result, people increasingly hesitate to accept kindness because they do not want to feel indebted. At the same time, the person offering help may expect gratitude, recognition or a favour in return.
sub.why.quoteHtml: Gest Dobra was created to remind us that kindness can happen without anyone having to settle a debt.
sub.why.title: Why Was Gest Dobra Created?
